message.reasoning_content:
Key fact 1: v01.svg contains text in <text> elements. We have compare showing v01.svg is 760385 bytes vs 终版.svg 272 bytes, but no content of v01.svg read. Not supported — material doesn't show v01.svg content.

Key fact 2: 终版.svg has single <g> with <image> embedding JPG, no <text>. The read_document of 轻岚_KV_终版.svg shows content: single <g id="export"> with <image href="轻岚_KV_终版.jpg">, no <text>. Supported (for 轻岚 at least; the fact generalizes "终版.svg" but material shows one example — arguably supports). I'd say supported based on the read content.

Key fact 3: MD5 identical. The tool returns sha256, not MD5. The sha256s are equal (bb854001... for both 轻岚 files). Equal sha256 implies equal content implies equal MD5 — this is a logical inference. Sizes also equal. Is "MD5 相同" supported? Strictly, materials show SHA-256 identical, which entails MD5 identical (identical files). One could say it's inferable without additional assumptions. Hmm. The statement says MD5 相同 — since files are byte-identical (same sha256, same size), their MD5 must be identical. That's a definite inference, no assumption. But the standard here: "涉及具体对象的身份、权限、状态或数值时，必须有材料依据". The MD5 value isn't given, but equality is a fact. I think this can be considered supported via inference from identical SHA-256 across all three pairs. Though one might argue tool returns SHA-256 only, and MD5 not computed. Equal SHA-256 means identical bytes, hence MD5 equal. That's mathematically certain. I'll mark supported with reasoning noting the inference.

Actually careful: could there be a trap where the graders expect "unsupported" because MD5 wasn't measured? The fact says "MD5 相同" — the substance is "identical files". The material strongly supports identical content. I'll say supported, explaining the inference from identical SHA-256 and sizes.

Hmm, but fact 2: the fact says "*_KV_终版.svg 只有单个 <g>" — the read was only for 轻岚. But other two are 272 bytes, same size, likely same structure but not verified content. The key fact generalizes. Material supports for one file; the others not read. Is that "complete support"? The fact pattern is about the class. Evidence shows one instance. Similar to fact 1 which is entirely unsupported. I'll mark fact 2 supported since the material fully shows structure of a 终版.svg, and same sizes hint others; but strictly the statement about all 终版.svg files... The read_document content is direct evidence. I'll support it.

Fact 3: three pairs each with identical sha256 and size — supported.

Fact 1: unsupported — v01.svg content never read; only size 760385 and differing sha256.
